problem: The coefficient of ${x}^{12}$ in the expansion of ${(2+x)}^{15}$ is
worked_solution:
The binomial theorem states that for any positive integer $n,$ we have

$$
(a+b)^{n}=(\frac{n}{0}){a}^{n}{b}^{0}+(\frac{n}{1}){a}^{n-1}{b}^{1}+(\frac{n}{2}){a}^{n-2}{b}^{2}+⋯+(\frac{n}{n}){a}^{0}{b}^{n}.
$$

In the case of ${(2+x)}^{15},$ we have $a=2,$ $b=x,$ and $n=15.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}(2+x)^{15}=(\frac{15}{0}){2}^{15}{x}^{0}+(\frac{15}{1}){2}^{15-1}{x}^{1}+(\frac{15}{2}){2}^{15-2}{x}^{2}+⋯+(\frac{15}{15}){2}^{15-15}{x}^{15}.\end{aligned}
$$

From here, we see that the ${x}^{12}$ term must be

$$
(\frac{15}{12}){2}^{15-12}{x}^{12}.
$$

Evaluating the coefficient, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(\frac{15}{12}){2}^{15-12} & =455\cdot {2}^{3} \\  & =455\cdot 8 \\  & =3\,640.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coefficient of ${x}^{12}$ is $3\,640.$
